nodes.name: validate_resume_proof

nodes.name: cool_down

nodes.name: state_digest

nodes.name: require_disk
nodes.summary: Raises unless the output filesystem has the required free GiB; never deletes or falls back.

nodes.name: require_resources

nodes.name: failure

nodes.name: statistics_json

nodes.name: SlotExhausted

nodes.name: BudgetExhausted

nodes.name: read_journal

nodes.name: substitutions_of

nodes.name: make_execute

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README frames the research question: how much and what kind of data a VLA needs to generalise, compared across SmolVLA and X-VLA fine-tuning on Franka Panda cube stacking and, later, props sorting. It also logs the results of each experiment axis. TODO.md shows what is currently open, so read both before diving into any code.

tour.title: Rules for Working Here
tour.description: This is a reproducibility-first research repo: datasets carry seals, training runs record bindings over source files, and a run refuses to start if it cannot reproduce them. The agent instructions encode the non-negotiables (never edit a hash-bound file during a run, never delete datasets, never weaken a gate), and AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md point to this single source of truth. The path-scoped experiments instructions apply the same rules to contracts, runners and SOURCE_FILES.
tour.languageLesson: Markdown instruction files with applyTo front-matter (like experiments.instructions.md) are loaded automatically by agent tooling only when an edited path matches the glob, which keeps rules scoped to the code they govern.

tour.title: Two Pinned Docker Images
tour.description: Everything runs inside digest-pinned images: an admission image (MuJoCo 3.13.0) for sealed packages and training, and a derived robosuite image (robosuite 1.5.2, MuJoCo 3.4.0) for anything that builds the robosuite scene. Results from the two are not physics-comparable. The base Dockerfile and compose services belong to the older SmolVLA/LIBERO workflow, while the robosuite Dockerfile shows how the second image derives from the first; OPERATIONS.md holds the flags, mounts and gate sequence.
tour.languageLesson: A Dockerfile pinned by digest (FROM image@sha256:...) is immutable, unlike a tag, which is what makes the environment itself part of the reproducibility claim. A derived Dockerfile adds one layer (robosuite) on top of the pinned base.

tour.title: Robot Model and Controllers
tour.description: The src/ tree defines the Franka Panda in MuJoCo MJCF/URDF and the controllers and planners that move it. The Panda config module is the most widely imported file in the repo (fan-in 55), supplying joint names, home configuration and scene path, while the wrapper, damped IK controller, joint-target limits, grasp controller and trajectory planner build the scripted expert from it. Every collection and evaluation package depends on this foundation.

tour.title: Shared Benchmark and Validation Helpers
tour.description: data_collection/benchmark.py is the most depended-on module (fan-in 61): timing configuration, state capture/restore and action validation shared by collectors and evaluators. pilot_plan and pilot_integrity define deterministic plans and integrity checks, while validation/gates.py provides verification gates such as dataset fingerprinting that refuse to pass without replay validation. These helpers are the common vocabulary of every later experiment package.

tour.title: Cube-Task Collection Packages
tour.description: Each experiment axis is a self-contained package; the plain-MuJoCo cube programme (pilot through B2) begins with fixed_layout. Its contract.py declares what is bound into the dataset seal, source.py and record.py drive the scripted-expert collection, and later packages such as bounded_placement_v3 and paired_demonstrations reuse them. The pattern of plan, expert, scenes, validate and seal repeats in every *_data package.
tour.languageLesson: In Python, a contract module that exposes SOURCE_FILES plus a provenance() function hashes the exact code that produced an artifact, so a later run can refuse to start if the code has drifted.

tour.title: Robosuite Scene (B3)
tour.description: The B3 stage rebuilds the cube task inside a robosuite-composed scene while keeping the repo robot contract. scene.py builds the model, xml_contract.py rewrites robosuite XML to match names, gains and force ranges, and cameras.py shares the front and gripper camera parameters. contract.py pins the image digests and versions, and the numbered gate tests (R1-R9) prove the new scene matches the old robot and cameras before anything is collected.

tour.title: Sealed B3 Collection
tour.description: The B3 collection package turns the robosuite scene into a sealed dataset of 500 training, 60 validation and 60 reserved layouts. plan.py draws deterministic seeded layouts, record.py runs a resumable journal with a rejection budget, validate.py admits episodes and fingerprints the dataset, and contract.py hashes every bound source file into the seal. Because the seal hashes these files and the scene code, they are frozen once sealed.

tour.title: Training Contract and Runner
tour.description: Training packages split into contract.py (what is bound: seal, plan, provenance, schedule, resume proof) and runner.py (what runs: check, preflight and train stages with snapshots and checkpointing). The X-VLA B3 package is the reference, and props P1 forks it with an instruction-to-task mapping. Their fork-hygiene tests catch residue from copying a package, which has let green suites coexist with broken code before.
tour.languageLesson: The fork-hygiene test uses Python symtable and AST inspection to find undefined names and stale package names statically, a cheap way to catch copy-paste residue without running the code.

tour.title: Props Scene and Scripted Expert
tour.description: The props scene replaces cubes with real-life objects sorted into two bins. constants.py fixes every spec number, scene.py builds the two-bin model, geometry.py measures prop extents from compiled collision geoms, and expert.py plans yaw-aware grasps and carries over bin walls, with metrics.py defining the in-bin success streak. P0 proved this expert on a 288-attempt gate before any data was collected, and its files are hashed by every later props seal.

tour.title: Props P1 and P2 Datasets
tour.description: P1 collected 540 instruction-sorting episodes, and P2 added one or two distractor objects. The P2 package subclasses the P0 expert with a higher carry height to clear standing distractors, collects in 12 parallel shards, then merges and verifies them. Its contract binds pinned images, shard count and disk floor, and its validation admits each episode against expert success, distractors, replay and labels.

tour.title: Rendering Verification: EGL versus OSMesa
tour.description: The experiments/egl_rendering package is not a dataset or training package: it has no contract or seal and nothing else hashes it. It adds one Docker image (the robosuite image plus libegl1) and the check that decides whether GPU EGL rendering can be admitted as a measurement instrument. check.py runs one unmodified props P1 attempt under a named renderer and refuses to run if MUJOCO_GL does not match its label; its report stage applies criteria C1 to C3 (OSMesa pixels unchanged, physics bit-identical, EGL repeatable). compare.py supplies the pure numpy comparisons and the C3 limits, and the dated report records the result. EGL is not adopted for any dataset or evaluation: the P2 checkpoints were trained on OSMesa pixels and need a paired test before any EGL evaluation.

tour.title: Evaluation Protocols
tour.description: Evaluation packages roll trained checkpoints on reserved layouts that never appeared in training. Each protocol.py defines screen, report and confirm tiers, feasibility.py runs the scripted expert on every layout first so unsolvable layouts are not blamed on the policy, and rollout.py runs the closed-loop trial. analysis.py classifies failures and computes layout-clustered intervals, since the independent unit is the layout, not the rollout.

tour.title: Failure Diagnostics
tour.description: When rollouts fail, the P2 diagnostics subpackage replays each recorded trial in the simulator, measures grasp geometry against an expert reference envelope, and classifies the failure with an ordered taxonomy. stats.py supplies permutation and Mann-Whitney tests so concentration claims are tested rather than eyeballed. This follows the repo rule that a timeout label is not a cause.

tour.title: Props P3: Food vs Drinks, a Failed Attempt
tour.description: P3 changed the instruction axis: one fixed prompt, "sort the item", and the policy must infer the category (drinks to the orange bin, food to the blue bin). experiments/props_p3_data collected and sealed 544 expert episodes of four trained objects (can, milk, bread, lemon); bottle and cereal were never collected, so they test generalisation. experiments/xvla_props_p3 forks the P2 training package with the instruction machinery re-derived for a single string, and experiments/xvla_props_p3_eval rolls the checkpoints on 288 reserved layouts after checking expert feasibility. The outcome was a failed attempt: the best checkpoint (101,520) scored 85.0% on trained objects (91.7%, 22/24, on the confirm tier) but only 5.7% on held-out objects, and the held-out criterion was not interpretable because the bottle never had a stable placement; failures were mostly never lifting the object (bottle) or choosing the wrong bin (cereal). The user closed P3 on 2026-10-27 and deleted its datasets and checkpoints (never published), so the two dated reports are the only record and the figures cannot be re-checked.

tour.title: Task Skills for Safe Operation
tour.description: Skills encode the procedures learned the hard way: launching a run with the --check/--preflight/--train sequence, collecting a dataset with rejection budgets and resume, evaluating a checkpoint, and diagnosing binding failures. The robosuite-path skill explains which image a command belongs in, and the branching skill prevents checkouts in bind-mounted directories. Read the relevant skill before starting any long run.

tour.title: Docs Map and Next Steps
tour.description: INDEX.md separates live ALL_CAPS documents from immutable dated reports. RESULTS.md holds every quoted figure, BENCHMARK_STATUS.md is the newest-first log, FAILURES.md records every costly mistake, and HUGGING_FACE_ARTIFACTS.md maps published datasets and checkpoints. The props P3 handoff shows where the programme goes next, and every finding must update these live docs in the same turn. To navigate the code itself, scripts/code_graph.py queries the generated .ua knowledge graph (status, layers, show, importers, find) without loading it whole. scripts/code_graph_bench.py is a read-only proxy that compares the context cost of answering the same navigation questions with the graph versus grep and checks the graph answers against grep.
